oracle.project: edge-g formula and canonical mediation examples
oracle.method: explicit enumeration of directed T-to-Y paths and recanting witnesses
oracle.independence_basis: reference.py is standard-library Python that imports no Antecedent code. For each case it enumerates every directed T -> Y path explicitly, marks a path selected when it visits every included node (empty list: all paths), and finds recanting witnesses W by the Avin-Shpitser-Pearl condition (a shared prefix to W with one selected and one unselected continuation to Y). It reproduces all seven statuses and checks the named witness is among the derived witnesses. The shared object is the recanting-witness definition and the selection convention (a path is selected when it visits all included nodes), both stated in the fixture and the query documentation; the product decides the same question by reachability, which the reference does not use.
oracle.historical_exposure: The cases and their expected statuses were written by hand from the recanting-witness definition together with a temporary harness that was not retained (recorded under historical_oracle). The retained reference was written during this review from the definition and the fixture cases with no product implementation source consulted; who first derived the expected statuses is unrecorded.

reference_review.limitations: Directed graphs only: the fixture states that the district-level criterion for latent confounding is not implemented. Seven small graphs. For selection_not_edge_closed the reference finds two witnesses (A and R) while the fixture and assertion name A; the assertion checks that the product's reported witness is the one named, which is a choice among valid witnesses and is not derived. The method string (path_specific.natural) is a repository label the reference does not derive. Identification status is a graph property; no estimation or calibration is involved.
reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 generator and deterministic inputs. Python standard library only, in an isolated locked script environment, outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source is stored.

cases.note: W lies on the selected T->A->W->Y and the unselected T->B->W->Y but is not a witness: the two paths leave T through different children, so W takes A from the active world and B from the control world
selecting T->W->Y leaves T->M1->W->Y unselected; W is on both but T's children M1 and W each start one kind of path only
L starts the selected T->L->M->Y and the unselected T->L->Y
W continues to the selected W->A->Y and the unselected W->B->Y after the shared prefix T->W
only T->A->R->Z->Y is selected; A also starts the unselected T->A->R->Y
